source.title: A jamming transition from under- to over-parametrization affects loss landscape and generalization
source.authors: Stefano Spigler; M. Geiger; Stéphane d'Ascoli; Levent Sagun; G. Biroli; M. Wyart

record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps fully connected network size and measures test error around the training-loss transition, using a setting and measure that bear on V2 but do not reproduce Neyshabur, Tomioka & Srebro's setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-error curves against network size for three MNIST training-set sizes. Values are presented in figures; the text describes their trends. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study varies fully connected ReLU network width and measures held-out error beyond the zero-training-loss transition, directly testing V2 in a different architecture and task setup. The pre-transition increase does not contradict V2's post-fitting claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the central result but omits the initial decrease: test error first decreases at small sizes, then rises to a cusp near jamming, then decreases monotonically and slowly beyond it. Selecting earlier training times removes the cusp, and the benefit of early stopping diminishes at large sizes.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses five-hidden-layer fully connected ReLU networks on MNIST reduced to 10 PCA components, a hinge loss, and fixed-step vanilla gradient descent; the specified comparison uses one-hidden-layer networks on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10.
record.method_sensitivity: The test-error trend changes with network size relative to the jamming transition; the reported transition and curves are also examined at different training-set sizes. Early stopping removes the cusp.

fits_no_version.finding: Final test error peaks near jamming, and choosing the minimum test error attained during training removes the cusp.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Test error can peak near the interpolation transition, with the peak depending on training duration and early stopping.

record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical
record.problems: Test-error curves are shown in figures without numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the text. MNIST inputs are reduced to 10 PCA components. The study uses a fixed training duration and notes that the minimum test error occurs before the end of training.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results left out.

untested.parts: No matched natural-label versus random-label experiment reporting both training fit and held-out accuracy; random-input fitting experiments do not establish the full coexistence claim.

The original one-hidden-layer setup, downsampled CIFAR-10, and the exact threshold for zero classification error are untested. Here N* is defined through zero hinge loss, which additionally requires a margin; training uses a finite step budget.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or manipulation of local connectivity.
No optimizer comparison with held-out performance.
No magnitude-aware perturbation measure or comparison of its ranking with generalization gaps.
No removal and retraining experiment involving memorized examples.

missing.what: Width-versus-test-error results for two-hidden-layer networks at P = 10k, 20k, and 50k, showing qualitatively similar post-jamming improvement.
missing.locator: Section 4, final paragraph; Appendix B.2, Details about Fig 4; Figure B2.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V2. The record's limits_scope verdict incorrectly treats nonmonotonicity across the entire width sweep as a qualification of a claim restricted to widths beyond fitting. The main text describes vanilla gradient descent, while the appendix gives Adam settings for hinge-loss experiments without clearly resolving their applicability to Figure 4; avoid asserting an unambiguous optimizer recipe.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not compare natural-label generalization with fitting random labels.
The study tests network-size effects on MNIST, but not the specified one-hidden-layer setup, downsampled CIFAR-10, or the claim's exact width threshold defined by zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-gap comparison.
